newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals were called to open mixed on Thursday, as gold and silver struggled to find some support, with the U.S. dollar remaining strong against most currencies overnight.
COMEX August gold was called to open up 50 cents to $1.00 an ounce from Wednesday's close at $318.70, after trading between $318.40 and $320.50 in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $319.60/00 early, compared to the London Thursday morning fix at $318.75 and the New York close Wednesday around $317.80/30.
COMEX gold stocks fell 12,254 ounces to 857,405 ounces in Wednesday's data, while COMEX silver stocks fell 34,437 ounces to 180,000,012 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening unchanged to up 1.0 cent from Wednesday's close at $4.185 an ounce, after trading in a $4.145-4.225 range in overnight ACCESS trade.

In London Thursday morning silver fixed at $4.2235 an ounce, a new three year low, after sliding to its lowest levels since November 1993 in the bullion market in late New York trade Wednesday, under pressure from fund selling.

NYMEX October platinum was seen opening unchanged to down $1.00 an ounce from Wednesday's close at $392.20, in line with some weakness in the bullion market in European trade, but platinum futures on the Tokyo Commodities Exchange (TOCOM) ended higher again overnight.
NYMEX September palladium was also seen opening unchanged to down $1.00 an ounce from Wednesday's close at $157.65 an ounce, but TOCOM palladium was also higher overnight.
Russian platinum group metals supplies resumed this week, after a suspension of six months.
